title: Realtime preemptible slot recovery - architecture scrub notes
body:
Meeting: Realtime preemptible slot recovery — architecture scrub
Date: 2026-02-20 10:00 PT
Attendees: Priya (owner, notes), Elliot, Mariana, Omar, Sophie, guests: infra-ops (Sam)
Purpose: Review RFC draft for handling preemptible GPU slot interruption in the realtime serving tier and agree on recovery semantics, SLO downgrade modes, and implementation boundaries between serving-runtime and platform-engineering.

Summary (top-line decisions):
- Adopt a two-stage recovery model: fast-reattach for interactive sessions (preferred for short conversations), and full-checkpoint restore for long-session continuity.
- Implement a lightweight slot-lease + tombstone marker in the model-hotstore so other workers can decide preemption vs. handoff quickly.
- Use NVMe-backed local checkpointing for KV-prefix snapshots (best-effort, TTL 5 minutes) to reduce cold-start token recomputation.
- Degraded mode: when fast-reattach fails, fall back to a reduced-compute variant (quantized or distilled model) for a bounded window (configurable per-tenant).

Discussion notes and rationale:
- Problem recap: Preemptible workers (spot GPUs) allow cost-effective capacity but lead to abrupt loss of KV caches and in-memory session state. Current behavior causes long tail latencies and high token recompute for active conversations.

- Two-stage recovery rationale:
  - Fast-reattach: attempt to rebind the session to a warm worker by shipping minimal session manifest + last-kv-page pointer. Target overhead <25ms in-path for routing decision. Works when another worker already has relevant model artifacts and policy allows migration.
  - Full-checkpoint restore: if fast-reattach can't find warm capacity, restore from local NVMe snapshot (if present) then replay last few tokens to rebuild transient caches. Accepts a longer latency (500ms–2s); bounded by checkpoint availability and shard throughput.

- Checkpointing policy:
  - Write frequency: in-memory incremental snapshots every 30s or after N token boundary (N=64) whichever comes first.
  - Storage: local NVMe (ephemeral) + optional background push to model-hotstore for tenants with high continuity SLAs.
  - TTL: 5 minutes default; TTL extended for dedicated capacity tenants to 1 hour.
  - Consistency: checkpoints are append-only segment files with a small manifest including model-version, kv-offset, and epoch tag. This avoids heavyweight atomic rename protocol.

- Slot-lease and tombstone marker:
  - Each slot holds a short-lived lease token written to shared etcd/lease-table. On preemption signal (or SIGTERM grace), slot writes a tombstone with last-known manifest. Other workers consult lease-table during routing to decide reattach vs. restore.
  - Leases are cheap: TTL 10s, auto-refresh while active. Tombstones persist for TTL+grace.

- Degraded model fallback:
  - When both reattach and checkpoint restore fail, allow policy-driven fallback to a compatible, smaller model variant for bounded time window (configurable per-tenant). This maintains throughput at cost of quality rather than dropping requests.
  - Platform must advertise variant compatibility matrix in the placement service to avoid silent semantic regressions.

- SLO and observable implications:
  - New SLO tiers required: continuity-SLO (probability of session preserved without full replay) and tail-latency-SLO for reattach path.
  - Instrumentation: counters for fast-reattach success, checkpoint-hit, degraded-fallback triggered, checkpoint-restore latency histogram. Add sampling traces for end-to-end reattach flow.

- Security and multi-tenant isolation:
  - Checkpoint manifests must be tenant-scoped and encrypted at rest. Local NVMe encryption with KMS key per-host is acceptable; platform-engineering to confirm host-level key separation for multi-tenant hosts.
  - Tombstones must not include PII or raw prompt text (only hashes + offsets).

Open questions / unresolved risks: 
- Race condition when two workers attempt to restore the same session from NVMe concurrently (costly replay duplication). Proposal: introduce a lightweight durable lock in lease-table to serialize actual restore operations. Need to quantify lock failure/backoff policy.
- Cold model artifact availability during reattach: if artifact pull latency is high, reattach becomes ineffective. Need tighter coupling with artifact prewarming policy in platform-engineering.
- NVMe eviction: on host churn, snapshots can disappear. Should we push every checkpoint to model-hotstore for mission-critical tenants? Cost analysis needed.
- Cost tradeoffs: checkpoint frequency vs. NVMe wear & cost. Ask finance for a rough estimate on storage + IO for expected traffic shapes.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Priya: update RFC with two-stage sequence diagrams, lease/tombstone schema examples, and reattach API contract (due 2026-02-27).
- Elliot: prototype lease-table lock logic and microbenchmark for reattach path (due 2026-03-06).
- Mariana: coordinate with platform-engineering on artifact prewarm policy and host KMS constraints; provide brief by 2026-03-03.
- Omar: add traces and metrics spec for reattach/restore paths to the observability backlog (open ticket JIRA-RT-3429) (due 2026-02-28).
- Sophie: run cost sensitivity exercise comparing checkpoint schedules (30s, 60s, 120s) and NVMe push strategies; present numbers 2026-03-10.

Compatibility boundaries & API notes: 
- Reattach API: session-manifest (session_id, model_version, kv_anchor, last_token_idx, tenant_id, session_hint). Response: (reattach_status: success|not-found|in-progress, target_worker_id, estimated-latency-ms).
- Checkpoint manifest schema example to live in RFC appendix (sha256, model_version, kv_segment_ids[], epoch, created_at).
- Placement service must export an endpoint to query warm workers by model-version and last-updated-epoch; the RFC will specify a 50ms budget for that RPC.

Testing plan: 
- Unit & integration tests for lease lifecycle and tombstone semantics.
- Chaos testing: scripted preemptions at 1–5% of active slots during load tests; measure reattach success and tail-latency impact.
- e2e perf: synthetic conversation workloads with mixed sequence lengths to evaluate checkpoint throughput and degraded fallback quality.

Notes to reviewers:
- This draft tries to balance operator cost with session continuity. The goal is not perfect state preservation but a predictable, tiered behavior that avoids catastrophic tail latencies.
- Please comment on the lease/tombstone TTLs and whether the two-stage model matches what infra can support for artifact prewarming.

Meeting adjourned 11:12 PT.
